canonical_topic: Option buyer vs. seller: transfer of risk and long/short volatility
definition: Option trading always involves a buyer and a seller; money is not created by the option, it is simply transferred from seller to buyer if the option pays off, funded by the premium the buyer paid up front.
core_idea: The buyer is described as long the option / long volatility because rare large price moves produce a big profit for them, while the seller is short the option / short volatility because the same rare moves produce a big loss for them.
key_points: The seller accepts the possibility of a large loss in exchange for receiving the premium up front.
If the option pays off, the seller must have the cash on hand to pay the buyer — the option itself creates no new money.
Buyer = long the option / long volatility (benefits from rare, large moves).
Seller = short the option / short volatility (harmed by rare, large moves).
relationships: Builds on the options overview and payoff formulas
trading_implications: Sellers of options are effectively compensated for bearing tail risk and need to be prepared to fund large payouts on rare adverse moves.
caveats: Thinking an option payoff represents new wealth creation rather than a transfer between two counterparties.
